title: Inside isomorphism and outside vanishing for an open-extension counit
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], $R$ its underlying sheaf of rings, $W\subseteq X$ an open, $S:\operatorname{Mod}(R|_W)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ any left adjoint to restriction with adjunction $a$, and $F$ a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $T_x$ for the stalk of the underlying abelian sheaf at $x\in X$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. If $x\in W$, then $T_x(a.\varepsilon_F)$ is an isomorphism; if $x\notin W$, then $T_x(S(F|_W))$ is a zero object. No covering or additivity assumptions on $S$ are required.

proof.text: Restriction has the right adjoint overPushforwardOverAdj. Over.forget W is fully faithful because opens form a thin category, hence Over.forgetAdjStar W has invertible unit. The right-adjoint counit is restriction along this unit and is therefore invertible on sections. Mathlib Adjunction.Triple.isIso_unit_iff_isIso_counit makes the specified extension/restriction unit invertible. The right triangle identity expresses the restricted counit as its inverse.

For x in W, whisker the underlying abelian presheaf counit with the image-open functor of W. Each component is the image under evaluation and forgetting of a restricted counit component, hence is invertible. Apply the stalk functor on W. The source and target restrictStalkIso comparisons conjugate this map to the global counit stalk map; prove the equality by stalk_hom_ext, restrictStalkIso_hom_eq_germ and stalkFunctor_map_germ. Cancel the source comparison to obtain the desired isomorphism.

For the outside clause, specialize localizedModule_adjunction_exact to the opens precoverage and X.sheaf, rewriting its generated Grothendieck topology to Opens.grothendieckTopology X. This yields an adjunction for the direct-sum module extension followed by sheafification. If x is outside W, every neighborhood V of x has no arrow V to W. The empty direct sum has only its zero element; representing stalk elements by germs proves the underlying presheaf stalk is zero. The stalk isomorphism induced by the sheafification unit transports this to the sheafified extension.

Apply Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq to the specified adjunction and the canonical extension adjunction, evaluate at the restriction of F, and map this isomorphism through the underlying abelian stalk functor. Transport the zero-object property using IsZero.of_iso. Only the outside clause needs this comparison.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00A7 (2)-(4); inside proof via the adjoint-triple criterion and restriction-stalk comparisons, outside by direct-sum germs and adjunction uniqueness

theorem open_extension_counit_stalk (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u})
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (_hR : R = (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj X.sheaf)
    (W : Opens X)
    (S : SheafOfModules.{u} (R.over W) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    (a : S ⊣ overFunctor.{u} R W) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (x : X) :
    let T := toSheaf R ⋙ TopCat.Sheaf.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u} X.carrier ⋙
      TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x
    (x ∈ W → IsIso (T.map (a.counit.app F))) ∧
      (x ∉ W → IsZero (T.obj (S.obj ((overFunctor.{u} R W).obj F))))
